title: Computer-aided design of functional whole genomes

concept.text: The innovation would be a dependable computer-aided system that turns explicit biological specifications into complete genome designs capable of supporting viable cells with the requested properties. The aim is to design substantially new arrangements of genetic information whose combined behavior works when the DNA is synthesized and placed in a suitable cellular environment. Producing a long sequence that resembles a natural genome is an intermediate achievement; viability and the specified functions require experimental demonstration.

Engineering interpretation: a successful design must coordinate genes, their regulation, genome replication, metabolism and compatibility with the recipient cell. These requirements interact: a collection of individually plausible genes does not by itself establish a functioning cellular system. A defensible initial scope is bacterial genomes in defined recipient cells and growth conditions. Designing functional eukaryotic genomes would extend the capability substantially and should be assessed separately.

significance.text: Conditional capability assessment: dependable specification-to-genome design would make whole-genome engineering programmable. Its direct consequence would be a systematic way to propose substantially different cellular architectures and, when combined with DNA synthesis and experimental testing, determine which architectures deliver the requested behavior. This would expand engineering from modifying selected parts of an existing genome toward designing the coordinated genetic system.

Manufacturing organisms or therapeutic applications would be downstream possibilities, contingent on physical implementation, suitable cellular environments and application-specific validation. A genome that sustains a cell in one laboratory setting does not establish useful production performance or clinical benefit. The analogy to compiling software is therefore limited: the physical cell, its starting machinery and its environment remain part of the functioning system. Successful genome design would not imply universal biological control or inevitable commercial or medical success.

missing_breakthrough.text: The target gap is the ability to move reliably from a requested cellular behavior to a complete genome that actually sustains replication and delivers that behavior. Computational measures of gene content, sequence similarity or predicted protein properties cannot establish this outcome on their own. The Evo 2 study illustrates the distinction: its genome-scale generations lacked important elements, including some essential genes, and its authors explicitly cautioned that their evaluation metrics did not establish functional or replication-competent genomes.

Engineering synthesis: the design system must account for interactions across the genome, including whether essential functions are present, whether their regulation is compatible, whether replication and metabolism can operate together, and whether the proposed genome works with the machinery available in the recipient cell. It must also connect explicit specifications to measurable outcomes, so that a viable design can be distinguished from one that achieves the requested function. Meeting these requirements across substantially different designs is a stronger capability than reproducing a nearly complete natural genome.

Physical implementation and experimental feedback are additional barriers. Genome-scale designs must be synthesized, introduced into suitable cells and tested through sustained growth, with failures informing subsequent designs. The Evo 2 authors describe experimental testing at this scale as requiring substantial iterative effort. The supplied evidence identifies these limitations in that study; it does not establish that every approach across the field remained unable to overcome them as of November 1, 2026.

current_state.text: In the Evo 2 study reported on March 4, 2026, the authors used a 10.5-kilobase segment of the Mycoplasma genitalium reference genome as a prompt to generate ten sequences of 580 kilobases each. This demonstrated sequence generation at the scale of a small prokaryotic genome. The generated sequences were annotated with Prodigal and evaluated computationally through gene annotations, sequence similarity and predicted protein properties.

Those results did not demonstrate viable whole genomes or sustained cellular replication directed by the generated sequences. The authors stated that the computational metrics did not guarantee functionality or replication competence, and that the generations lacked important elements, including some essential genes. These are substantive limitations of the reported designs, rather than merely an absence of experimental reporting. The paper separately described experimental validation of smaller chromatin designs; that narrower achievement does not establish the functionality of its whole-genome generations.

The supplied review reports that the saved HTML directly supports the generation dimensions and the authors’ limitations. It contains the full main article and references without reported extraction truncation; linked supplementary files and figure images were not inspected. A PDF retained alongside that HTML was identified as a different 2022 paper, Non-identifiability and the Blessings of Misspecification in Models of Molecular Fitness, and had extraction warnings. That PDF provides no evidence for the Evo 2 results, but its misassociation does not undermine the supporting HTML.

Evidence boundary: the supplied record contains no bounded search documenting subsequent developments through November 1, 2026. The March 2026 study therefore establishes a dated advance and its study-specific limitations, while the field-wide status at that later cutoff remains unresolved. This lack of freshness evidence does not show that later progress occurred or that the reported result is false.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: begin with explicit specifications for several substantially different bacterial genome designs, generate the designs prospectively, synthesize them and demonstrate sustained replication together with the requested distinct functions in suitable recipient cells. The reported Evo 2 gap motivates physical testing of complete designs; the particular demonstration requirements here are proposals, not published consensus standards.
completion_criteria.label: Prospectively designed bacterial genomes sustain replication and distinct requested functions

completion_criteria.text: Proposed evaluation definitions: before testing, specify quantitative criteria for sustained replication, functional performance, design diversity and dependence on natural reference genomes. The criteria should distinguish substantial genome design from copying an almost complete natural genome, without treating all reuse of natural sequence as disqualifying. No numerical thresholds are established by the supplied evidence, so none are asserted here.
completion_criteria.label: Predefined quantitative criteria distinguish substantial genome design from copying

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility requirement: independent teams should test multiple designs using sufficiently documented specifications, sequences, recipient cells and experimental conditions. They should report failures as well as successes, allowing readers to assess reliability across designs rather than only the performance of selected examples. Successful finite tests would establish demonstrated breadth within the tested organisms, functions and environments; they would not establish literal universality.
completion_criteria.label: Independent teams test multiple designs and report successes and failures

completion_criteria.text: Proposed practical boundary: report which recipient cells and growth conditions are required, whether the requested function persists during the demonstrated replication period, and what support the cellular environment supplies. Bacterial success would establish the initial capability within those boundaries. Extension to functional eukaryotic genomes would require additional evidence, while manufacturing or therapeutic claims would require their own application-specific demonstrations.
completion_criteria.label: Report cellular support requirements and functional persistence during replication

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: BIF-13, Predictive design of functional genetic circuits and pathways, is the closest overlap. It concerns coordinated genetic components operating within an existing host cell; BIF-05 concerns the complete genome and the viability of the resulting cellular system. Circuit and pathway design could contribute to whole-genome design, but successful components alone do not resolve genome-wide compatibility.

Roster-based synthesis: BIF-01, A predictive decoder for the regulatory genome, could help determine how a proposed genome controls gene activity. BIF-06, A general decoder for unknown gene and protein functions, could help identify what its components do. BIF-09, Proteome-scale prediction of molecular interactions and affinities, could inform whether their products interact appropriately. Each supplies potentially useful component-level knowledge; none alone demonstrates a complete viable genome.

Roster-based synthesis: BIF-02, Predictive molecular dynamics from biological sequence, concerns molecular behavior, whereas BIF-03, A transferable, predictive virtual cell, concerns prediction at the cellular level. Both could support evaluation of genome designs. BIF-04, General reconstruction of causal cellular networks, addresses the dependencies that a designer would need to understand or accommodate. These predictive and explanatory capabilities remain distinct from generating, synthesizing and validating a complete functional genome.

Roster-based synthesis: BIF-07, Computational reconstruction of organism-scale molecular maps, could provide broader biological context for genome design. BIF-08, Reliable reconstruction and forecasting of single-cell fates, could help evaluate resulting cell states, particularly in future eukaryotic extensions. Their primary goals concern mapping and forecasting biology rather than specifying an entire genome that produces a requested cellular behavior.

Roster-based synthesis: BIF-11, Accessible, uncertainty-aware assembly of complex genomes, reconstructs genome sequences from evidence; BIF-05 designs sequences to meet prospective specifications. Reliable assemblies could supply reference material and reveal uncertainty relevant to design, but reconstructing an existing genome and designing a new functional one are separate achievements. BIF-12, Strain-resolved discovery and functional profiling of microbial communities, concerns identifying and characterizing organisms within communities, whereas BIF-05 focuses on the genome of a designed cell.

Roster-based synthesis: BIF-10, A broadly capable autonomous bioinformatics discovery system, could coordinate genome-design proposals, computational analysis and experimental feedback. It describes a broader discovery capability; whole-genome design is a specific scientific and engineering outcome that such a system might pursue. Autonomy would not substitute for demonstrating genome function.

change_log.change: Preserved BIF-05 and its title while expanding the concept into specification-driven, experimentally functional whole-genome design.
change_log.reason: Integrates the candidate and research explanation with the review’s distinction between plausible sequences and viable cellular systems.

change_log.change: Qualified claims that the capability remained unavailable across the field.
change_log.reason: The supplied evidence establishes Evo 2’s March 2026 limitations, while no bounded freshness search establishes field-wide status as of November 1, 2026.

change_log.change: Added the reported generation dimensions: ten 580-kb sequences from a 10.5-kb M. genitalium prompt, together with the computational evaluation methods.
change_log.reason: The validated review identifies direct support in the saved HTML, making the scale and nature of the achievement clearer.

change_log.change: Added the absence of some essential genes and distinguished whole-genome generations from experimentally tested smaller chromatin designs.
change_log.reason: Preserves the review’s scientific distinctions and prevents narrower experimental success from being mistaken for whole-genome functionality.

change_log.change: Removed the unverified first-pass and reCAPTCHA history and explained the relevant source limitations.
change_log.reason: The supplied artifacts support the HTML evidence directly, while the retained PDF belongs to a different paper and cannot establish Evo 2 results or archive-access history.

change_log.change: Expanded completion criteria with advance operational definitions, independent testing, failure reporting and explicit experimental boundaries.
change_log.reason: Makes the proposed demonstration assessable without inventing numerical thresholds or presenting proposals as consensus standards.

change_log.change: Separated direct capability gains from conditional manufacturing and therapeutic possibilities.
change_log.reason: Whole-genome programmability would not by itself establish application performance, clinical benefit or universal biological control.

change_log.change: Explained relationships with every other supplied roster entry while retaining BIF-13 as the closest overlap.
change_log.reason: Shows how supporting predictive, reconstructive and autonomous capabilities relate to whole-genome design without merging their distinct objectives.

unresolved_issues: The supplied record does not establish field-wide progress after the March 2026 Evo 2 report through November 1, 2026.
Quantitative thresholds for sustained replication, functional success, design diversity and dependence on natural reference genomes remain to be defined for a concrete demonstration.
The supplied evidence does not resolve which recipient cells, environments or breadth of requested functions a successful future system could support.
Linked supplementary files and figure images were not inspected in the supplied review; the retained PDF is a different paper with extraction issues and cannot fill those evidentiary gaps.
Functional eukaryotic genome design remains a separate extension whose completion requirements are not established by this bacterial demonstration proposal.

brief.title: Designing a cell’s complete DNA to order
possible: Researchers could specify what a bacterial cell should do and use a computer to design its genome, its complete set of DNA instructions. Once built and placed in a suitable cell, that DNA would keep the cell reproducing and performing the requested task.
why: This would let researchers design a cell’s coordinated genetic system instead of changing selected parts. They could explore substantially different ways of organizing cellular life and test which designs deliver the behavior they want.

sources.who: Garyk Brixi, Matthew G Durrant and collaborators
sources.showed: Their AI model generated DNA sequences as long as a small bacterial genome. Computer assessments found plausible features, but the designs lacked some essential genes and did not demonstrate living, reproducing cells.
sources.cited_for: Computer generation can reach the length of a whole bacterial genome.
sources.not_established: The generated DNA has not been shown to sustain a cell or deliver requested functions.

sources.who: Clyde A. Hutchison III, Ray-Yuan Chuang and collaborators
sources.showed: The team designed, built and tested a reduced bacterial genome that supported living cells. Repeated testing revealed genes needed for robust growth.
sources.quote:
An initial
design, based on collective knowledge of molecular biology combined with limited
transposon mutagenesis data, failed to produce a viable cell.
sources.cited_for: A designed and chemically built bacterial genome can support life when placed in a suitable cell.
sources.not_established: Reducing an existing genome does not establish dependable computer design of substantially different genomes for requested functions.

shown: Hutchison and collaborators built a reduced bacterial genome that supported living cells after repeated design and testing. Those cells depended on a nutrient-rich growth medium.

The Evo 2 team generated DNA at the scale of a small bacterial genome. These sequences underwent computer assessment, but lacked some essential genes. The team did not demonstrate that they could sustain living cells.
missing: A dependable system must turn requested cell behavior into complete DNA designs that work when built.
Several substantially different designs must sustain cell reproduction and deliver their distinct requested functions.
Testing must establish reliability across designs, with failures feeding back into better designs.

milestones.label: Designed bacterial genomes sustain reproduction and requested functions
milestones.explanation: Several substantially different bacterial genomes designed from explicit specifications would have to sustain reproduction and deliver distinct requested functions. This would connect computer design to working cells.

milestones.label: Measurable standards distinguish design from near copying
milestones.explanation: Criteria set before testing would have to measure reproduction, function, design diversity and reliance on natural genomes. This would distinguish substantial design from near copying while allowing reuse of natural DNA.

milestones.label: Independent teams establish reliability across multiple designs
milestones.explanation: Independent teams would have to test multiple designs with documented specifications, DNA sequences, recipient cells and conditions, reporting failures and successes. This would reveal reliability beyond selected examples.

milestones.label: Cellular support and lasting function are established
milestones.explanation: Tests would have to establish required recipient cells, growth conditions, environmental support and persistence of function during reproduction. This would define where the bacterial capability works.

uncertain: The quantitative thresholds for reproduction, functional success, design diversity and reliance on natural DNA remain undefined.
Which recipient cells, environments and requested functions could a dependable system support?
Success with bacteria would leave open how to design functional genomes for cells with a nucleus.
